correctness.rationale: Campbell/Tonelli and independent Poisson thinning give mu+=(rho_L/2)(V+m_L M), mu-=(rho_R/2)(V-m_R M) and Skellam net transfer. Conditioning the telegraph displacement on the Poisson number of flips and Dirichlet holding-time fractions gives V=vt exp(-x)(I0+I1); E X_t=M=v(1-e^-2x)/(2gamma), and derivatives V_prime=v exp(-x)I0, M_prime=v exp(-2x). The current sign reduces to strictly increasing Delta e^x I0+P, so exactly one x_J when P<-Delta. R=M/V=sinh(x)/[x(I0+I1)] decreases strictly 1->0 by I1<=xI0/2 and e^(2x)-1>2x+2x²; hence unique later x_Q. Standard modified Bessel expansions give x_J=0.5L+0.25log L+0.25log pi+o(1), x_Q~pi/(8c²). Independently numerically checked ratio monotonicity at 100 points and source Beta-mixture checker logic. This is endpoint transfer, not repeated path crossings.

value.rationale: Density imbalance and initial directional polarization are separately natural active-matter driving mechanisms. An adverse alignment generates a transient uphill mean current, followed by an independently delayed integrated-mass sign change; the exact necessary-and-sufficient inequality and parametrically different crossing scales constitute a complete physically motivated phase classification. No assertion about individual sample paths reversing at deterministic times.

final_claim: For independent telegraph particles in two Poisson half-line clouds with rho_L>rho_R and mean signs m_L,m_R, endpoint net transfer is Skellam, J=v/2[Delta e^-x I0(x)+P e^-2x] and EQ=(Delta V+P M)/2. Exactly when P<-Delta it has unique current reversal x_J and later unique cumulative-transfer reversal x_Q, with x_J~(1/2)log(1/c) and x_Q~pi/(8c²) as c=Delta/(-P)->0.
